hypothesis: London institutional flow systematically breaks the prior Asian session H1 rolling high/low for XAUUSD. This hypothesis is falsified if net expectancy R <= 0 after costs in the development period, or if fewer than 100 trades occur per period, or if no consistent directional edge appears across year and volatility regime splits.

mechanism.edge_should_disappear_when: Asian session was already highly directional (no range to break); major scheduled macro events coincide with London open (FOMC, NFP, CPI); rollover-period spread spikes; unusually high overnight volatility.
mechanism.edge_should_exist_when: Asian session forms a well-defined consolidation range; London open sees clean directional order flow beyond the Asian extremes with no major macro event coinciding.
mechanism.who_provides_opportunity: Asian session participants (regional central banks, jewelry-demand hedgers, low-volume market makers) who consolidate price in a narrow range under thin conditions; London institutional desks (macro funds, bank commodity desks, ETF arbitrageurs) who initiate directional positions at session open relative to overnight levels under benchmark and fix-execution mandates.
mechanism.why_it_may_persist: Institutional mandate-driven execution windows (AM London fix, benchmark rebalancing, compliance constraints) cannot be fully randomized. The pattern's reward-per-trade is too small relative to gold's spread and impact costs for pure arbitrage to eliminate it at scale.

title: Asian Range Breakout at London Open (XAUUSD H1)
